requirements.statement: The main import reason page's h1 reads 'Main import reason', its browser title 'Main import reason - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and the overview task row that links to it reads 'Main import reason'.
requirements.why: The prototype names the page 'Main import reason' and wins by default on a page name; no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-063 and repo-frontend-p8-064 show the heading and title reading 'Main import reason' today, and repo-tests-p1-056 and repo-tests-p1-072 show the tests repo asserting that wording for the page and its overview row. The fit and E2E traces, captured at the older animals frontend commit 4c2119da, still show 'Main reason for import' (trace-animals-fit-p7-003, trace-e2e-p4-079): they are a stale snapshot, not work left to do.

requirements.statement: The main import reason page shows the caption 'About the consignment' above its h1, and the question 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' is the reason radio group's visually hidden legend rather than a heading.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service already agree: the page heading stands as the question, and screen-reader users hear the legend as the group's name.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-063 shows the heading above a section caption with the question kept as a legend only screen readers reach, and trace-animals-fit-p7-004 gives the caption's words.

requirements.statement: Both pages sit in the journey layout: a Back link, a strip with a 'Draft' status tag and the notification reference above the caption, and on error a 'There is a problem' error summary between that strip and the caption.
requirements.why: The target design renders both pages this way and the real service already does; the shell area owns the layout itself.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-010-m1 and trace-animals-fit-p12-061 show the Draft strip; trace-animals-fit-p7-059 shows the error summary above the caption.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the main import reason is one radio choice of five reasons, in this order: Internal market; Transhipment or onward travel; Transit; Re-entry; Temporary admission horses. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, only one reason is held, no reason is pre-selected on a notification without one, and the list is the same for every live-animal commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the page carries its own two-reason list of Internal market and Transit.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service all offer the same five reasons in the same order, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which of them the germinals journey offers. The 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set with its own catalogue, so the reduced list belongs to that set's copy of the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-065 and repo-frontend-p8-071 show the five reasons in the service's order today, and repo-tests-p1-059 shows none pre-selected. The radio labels come from the shared import-reason-purpose service rather than the page's own copy file (repo-frontend-p8-072), so that is where a label changes. The policy page marks the reason field block 'At least one' while the field itself is a single-select enumeration and no field records a second reason (confluence-6497338582-p3-006): the single-select reading is what both the prototype and the real service build, so one reason is held.

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
requirements.why: The five hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-066 to repo-frontend-p8-070 hold the same five hints today, in the page's own copy file.

requirements.statement: A main import reason is optional to proceed: Save and continue with no reason chosen shows no error and moves on.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the reason mandatory to submit but lets the trader move past the page without it, the target design makes it optional to proceed, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-109 shows the reason itself is not a required answer on the page, and repo-tests-p1-071 shows a seeded draft left with no reason. No fit or page test submits the page with nothing chosen (repo-frontend-p8-109, trace-animals-fit-p7-076), so a test should pin it.

requirements.statement: Each reason that needs follow-up questions opens them in a standard GOV.UK conditional reveal directly under its own radio, so the reason and its follow-ups are answered in one submit; Re-entry has no reveal and saves on its own; every reveal is hidden until its reason is chosen. Without JavaScript every reveal shows open and the page still works, because only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved.
requirements.why: The target design asks the follow-ups as reveals on the reason page; the real service moved them there in DR1 parity (inc-067), so it already matches. The policy page names no extra field for Re-entry. The 9 October afternoon ruling requires every page to work fully without JavaScript, which GOV.UK's conditional reveal already gives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-091 shows no follow-up shown until a reason that needs one is chosen and the Re-entry radio controlling nothing, repo-frontend-p8-090 shows Re-entry saving alone, and repo-frontend-p8-120 shows the page working without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: Choosing Internal market reveals the radio question 'Purpose in the internal market' (medium legend) with eleven options, in this order: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift; Transfer of ownership - Rescue; Breeding; Research; Racing, competition, show or training; Approved premises or body; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming; Production; Slaughter; Fattening; Restocking. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, no purpose is pre-selected when the reveal first opens, and in the live-animals set all eleven are offered for every commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the reveal offers four: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service ask the same purpose question with the same eleven options in the same order for live animals, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which four the germinals journey offers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-073 and repo-frontend-p8-074 show the legend and the eleven purposes today, and repo-tests-p1-061 shows none pre-selected when the reveal first opens. The purpose labels come from the shared import-reason-purpose service rather than the page's copy file (repo-frontend-p8-086).

requirements.statement: Each of the eleven internal market purposes carries its own hint beneath its label: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift describes any movement aimed at sale or transfer of ownership, including gifts; Transfer of ownership - Rescue rehoming, adoption or fostering; Breeding reproduction and breeding programmes; Research 'Animals for use in scientific or medical research.'; Racing, competition, show or training 'Animals to participate in competitive or training events.'; Approved premises or body 'Animals for exhibition, zoos, collections, or conservation programmes where a licence or approval is needed.'; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming privately owned animals that cannot meet the non-commercial rules; Production 'Animals that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'; Slaughter 'Animals to be slaughtered and processed for meat production shortly after arrival into Great Britain.'; Fattening 'Animals to be fattened for meat production.'; Restocking 'To replenish or enhance populations of species, for example, restocking of game or fish.'
requirements.why: The eleven purpose hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-075 to repo-frontend-p8-085 hold the same eleven hints today.

The policy page gives no error wording for this section (confluence-6497338582-p3-068), so the service's own messages stand.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-088 shows port of exit then destination country today, both labelled as the ruling words them (repo-frontend-p8-093).

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-094 shows both lists served from the reference services rather than typed into the page, and trace-animals-fit-p7-075 shows every option arriving server-rendered with no browser-side lookup.

requirements.statement: The transhipment and transit 'Destination country' questions offer reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries plus their subdivisions, each subdivision labelled '<territory> (<parent>)', all sorted alphabetically as the origin page sorts them, and a chosen subdivision is stored by its own code. The content is what reference-data serves: trade-imports-stub locally and in CDP dev, real MDM in CDP test. No entry is added, removed or respelt in code.
requirements.why: The target design offers EU outermost regions and territories beside the countries, labelled with their parent, and the policy page has the destination country list come from MDM. The 9 October ruling lifts DR1's MDM block, because no reference list waits on MDM: the list is built now against reference-data as it is. It also rules that list content is MDM's to own, not the prototype's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-094 shows every country and subdivision named with its country, repo-frontend-p8-113 shows a territory chosen, stored by its own code and offered back named with its country, and repo-tests-p1-067 shows the tests repo reading subdivision codes. The fit specs prove the lists against captured master-data fixtures rather than a live service (repo-frontend-p8-149), and which upstream serves a real user cannot be read from these pages (repo-frontend-p8-150). The fit and E2E traces at the older commit still show 31 countries and no subdivisions (trace-animals-fit-p7-044, trace-e2e-p4-106).

requirements.statement: Every 'Port of exit' question on the main import reason page opens on 'Select one', with the ports following straight after and no divider line.
requirements.why: The target design's placeholder is 'Select one' with no divider, and it wins by default on this copy with nothing to override it. The 9 October afternoon ruling has how a list reads follow the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-093 shows the question opening on 'Select one' today, and repo-tests-p1-066 shows the same first option without JavaScript. The traces at the older commit still show 'Select port of exit' and a disabled divider (trace-animals-fit-p7-045, trace-e2e-p4-108).

requirements.statement: The transit and temporary admission 'Port of exit' questions both offer the whole ports-of-entry list from trade-imports-reference-data, the same list the port of entry question uses. Entries appear as MDM serves them, duplicates and misspellings included: these go to the MDM team as a data report, are not corrected in code, and no test pins them.
requirements.why: The policy page has the trader choose the port of exit from the port of entry list, because exit and entry share the same list of ports, and has that list come from MDM. The target design gives exit its own list of animal-approved border control posts; the 9 October ruling replaces that for now, because MDM carries no approved-for-animals flag. It also rules that the duplicate and misspelt ports are MDM's real data.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-094 shows the port of exit question offering every port, served from the reference service; trace-animals-fit-p7-045 and trace-e2e-p4-108 show both exit questions carrying the same 78-entry ports-of-entry list. Its labels and order change under their own requirements, and any test that pins a misspelt or duplicated name stops doing so (ruling claim 171).

requirements.statement: The exit date is one text field using the MOJ date picker, labelled 'Exit date' with a 'Choose date' calendar (Monday-first weeks, picking a day fills the field as day/month/year); the open calendar never covers the question below it, surrounding spaces are trimmed before the date is read, no earliest or latest date is set, and a date chosen from the calendar is saved and offered back in the field.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service use the same picker, label and calendar, and the policy page sets no bound on the exit date beyond its format. The MoJ date picker is one of the components the 9 October afternoon ruling accepts, the interaction designer confirms it as the picker every other date in both frontends uses, and design question 12 covers only the germinal dates read from a document, so the exit date keeps its calendar.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-096 shows the picker, its label and its 'Choose date' button, repo-frontend-p8-097 the saved date offered back, repo-frontend-p8-098-m1 the calendar never covering the question below, and repo-frontend-p8-111-m1 the trimming. Nothing in the tests repo asserts the field's label, hint or validation (repo-tests-p1-069). The hint wording and the typed form the field accepts are settled separately.

requirements.statement: With Transhipment or onward travel chosen and no listed destination country, Save and continue is refused with 'Select a destination country' in the error summary and inline on the question, which takes the GOV.UK error style; the reveal stays open and any port already chosen is kept.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the destination country mandatory to proceed once its condition is met, the target design requires it, and the real service already refuses with this message.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-101 holds the rule, the message, the open reveal and the kept port today; no fit or E2E trace submits transhipment without a country (trace-animals-fit-p7-077, trace-e2e-p4-122), so a test should pin it.

requirements.statement: With Transit chosen, a missing port of exit shows 'Select a port of exit' and a missing destination country 'Select a destination country', both together when both are missing, port first, each in the summary and inline; the reveal stays open and an answered field is kept.
requirements.why: The policy page makes both transit follow-ups mandatory to proceed, the target design requires them in this order, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-102 and repo-frontend-p8-103 show both messages named at once in the summary and in the open reveal, and trace-animals-fit-p7-064 shows their order.

requirements.statement: With Temporary admission horses chosen, a blank exit date shows 'Enter an exit date' and a missing port 'Select a port of exit', both together when both are missing, date first, each in the summary and inline; the reveal stays open, an answered field is kept and the summary link moves focus to the date box.
requirements.why: The policy page makes the exit date and port of exit mandatory to proceed once their condition is met, the target design requires both in this order, and the real service already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-104 holds both messages and repo-frontend-p8-105 the kept port and the focus move; trace-animals-fit-p7-069 shows their order.

requirements.statement: An exit date that is not a real calendar date (for example 31/2/2026) is refused with 'Enter a real date', in the summary and inline, with the typed value kept in the field; a past or future date is not refused.
requirements.why: The target design checks only that the exit date is present and real, the policy page sets no bound beyond the format, and the real service applies the same two rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-104 holds the 'Enter a real date' rule today, but no trace types an exit date by hand (trace-animals-fit-p7-078) and nothing in the tests repo asserts its validation (repo-tests-p1-069), so a test should pin it and confirm the typed value is redisplayed.

requirements.statement: When the reason page is shown again after a refused submit, the chosen reason stays selected with its reveal open, the other reveals stay hidden, and the user's entries are shown again.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service both re-render the page with the user's answers in place, and the 26 October ruling holds that what a trader typed is never dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-101 and repo-frontend-p8-105 show the reason kept checked, its reveal open and the answers the trader did give kept on a refused submit.

requirements.statement: Only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved; changing the reason removes the earlier reason's answers that the new one does not ask, so returning to Internal market after switching away offers no purpose and asks for it again.
requirements.why: The target design clears follow-up answers that belong to reasons no longer chosen, and the real service already purges them on save.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-099 shows only the chosen reason's questions checked and saved, and repo-frontend-p8-112 the purge when the reason changes.

requirements.statement: The notification holds one destination country, one port of exit and one exit date answer, each reached through its own form field per reveal, and every reveal that asks for it is prefilled from the saved answer, so a Transit country is still offered under Transhipment.
requirements.why: The target design names a separate field per reveal, but DR1 judged that the per-branch names are a DOM artefact, not extra questions, and that carrying a shared answer between reveals is not a requirement (inc-067); that judgement on the same difference stands. The policy page holds the answers at notification level.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-111 shows the destination country, the port of exit and the exit date each held as one answer whatever reason asked for them, and trace-e2e-p4-117 shows them prefilled in every reveal.

requirements.statement: The reason, internal market purpose, certification purpose and unweaned answers are stored as the service's codes (for example internalMarket, breeding, further-keeping, yes), not as their displayed labels.
requirements.why: Stored values are a persistence contract with the backend and other services that the prototype, which stores labels, cannot express; the ruling lets that constraint override the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-070 shows the reasons answered as internalMarket, transit and temporaryAdmissionHorses, repo-tests-p1-178 the unweaned answer posted as yes or no, and trace-animals-fit-p12-007 the kebab-case certification codes.

requirements.statement: A submitted reason, certification purpose or unweaned value that is not one of the offered options is refused with 'Select a valid option', linking to and focusing the group's first radio, with no option left checked and the other question's valid answer kept; a refused submit writes nothing to the notification.
requirements.why: Server-side validation that refuses tampered values and never saves a refused submit is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (it silently drops or stores them), so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-108, repo-frontend-p8-134 and repo-frontend-p8-135 show the refusal, the focus move, no option left checked and the other answer kept; trace-animals-fit-p12-027 and trace-animals-fit-p7-060 give the message's words, and trace-e2e-p4-115-m1 shows nothing written on a refused submit.

requirements.statement: When either page is refused on submit, the browser title is prefixed 'Error: ' and the page is answered with HTTP 400; each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: The 'Error: ' title prefix is how GOV.UK tells screen-reader users a validation error has happened; the prototype's title omits it, but accessible validation is a real constraint the prototype does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-119 and repo-frontend-p8-142 show the bad-request status on both pages, and trace-animals-fit-p7-059 and trace-animals-fit-p12-029 the 'Error: ' prefix.

requirements.statement: When a saved destination country, port of exit or certification purpose is no longer in the reference list, reopening the page says so ('The saved destination country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', 'The saved port of exit is no longer available. Select a port from the list.', 'The certification purpose you chose is no longer offered. Select a purpose from the list.') and blanks it in every reveal that asks for it; a saved purpose or exit date is not re-checked this way.
requirements.why: A saved answer going stale against reference data is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real service keeps handling it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-106 and repo-frontend-p8-136 hold the three messages, repo-frontend-p8-112-m1 the blanking in every reveal and repo-frontend-p8-107 that only the country and port answers are re-checked; no fit test exercises any of them (repo-frontend-p8-148).

requirements.statement: If saving either page fails, the page is shown again with the user's entries and the shared recoverable-error message, with HTTP 500.
requirements.why: A failed save is a persistence condition the prototype cannot express; the real service already recovers from it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-119 and repo-frontend-p8-142 show a failed save showing the page again in a recoverable-error state with a server-error status.

requirements.statement: The main import reason page's Back link goes to the previous journey page, What are you importing, and to the notification overview when the page was opened from the overview.

The builder changes only the linear-journey case.

requirements.statement: Both pages end with a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification overview.
requirements.why: The target design gives both pages the three journey controls, and the real service already has them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-116, repo-tests-p1-176-m1 and repo-tests-p1-177 show all three controls, and trace-animals-fit-p7-050 to trace-animals-fit-p7-052 show them rendered.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason page makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue', and differs only in where it goes when every answer passes: the notification overview rather than the next journey page. A missing or invalid follow-up answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, the chosen reason still checked, its reveal open and the entries shown again. When amending, the 'Save and return' (review) action makes the same checks and goes to the review page.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling, which outranks every other source, makes Save and return to overview run exactly the checks Save and continue runs, with an error for each missing or invalid answer and the trader kept on the page, and says no page is an exception; it replaces the earlier soft save recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313. The germinal-products set's copy of this page is a sibling set in the same frontend with the same two buttons, so it takes the same rule even though the ruling names only live animals and high-risk plants (ruling claim 24).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-117 shows the button making the same checks as Save and continue, so a missing follow-up refuses both the same way, and repo-frontend-p8-116 shows it saving and showing the overview; repo-tests-p1-060 shows the end-to-end suite using it. The 26 October ruling recorded that the button once skipped those checks (ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001), and no fit or E2E trace in this area exercises it (trace-animals-fit-p7-079).

requirements.statement: The main import reason page is walked only as part of a notification: no template-mode behaviour, Back link or save message is built on it.
requirements.why: Templates are out of this programme's work. The owner parked the templates rows in their own theme on 4 November and said they are not built now, Sam called Design Release 2.1's templates concept work rather than deadline work on 9 November, and the interaction designer recorded templates dropped for now; those later rulings outrank the 9 October templates ruling that had template mode walking this page, and they outrank the goal's mention of templates. The target design's template editing of this page is set aside with them.

requirements.statement: The main import reason task counts as complete once a reason allowed for the notification is saved with valid follow-ups (Internal market an allowed purpose; Transhipment a listed country; Transit a listed port and country; Temporary admission horses a real exit date and listed port; Re-entry nothing more), whether or not Additional details is answered; with no reason saved it is not complete.
requirements.why: The target design judges the reason section on its own answers and has Additional details as a separate task.
requirements.deltaNote: The E2E traces show the 'Main reason for import' row completing only once the Additional details page after it is saved too (trace-e2e-p4-112, trace-e2e-p4-116), while the fit traces at an older commit showed it complete on the reason alone (trace-animals-fit-p7-054). The page now weighs each of its own five answers against its own obligation (repo-frontend-p8-121) and Additional details no longer follows it in the journey, so the builder confirms the coupling is gone rather than assuming it.

requirements.statement: The additional details page is headed 'Additional details' (title 'Additional details - Import notification service - GOV.UK') with the caption 'Commodity details', and that is also the name of its overview task row.
requirements.why: The target design and the real service already agree on the heading, title and caption.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-125 shows the heading above its section caption, repo-tests-p1-170 the heading and task row name, and trace-animals-fit-p12-001 and trace-animals-fit-p12-002 the title and the caption's words. The page stays at /additional-details, not the prototype's /additional-animal-details path, because no increment changes a real URL path to match the prototype (ruling claim 72).

requirements.statement: The additional details page asks 'What are the animals certified for?' (medium legend) as radios with sixteen options and no hints, in this order: Further keeping; Slaughter; Confined establishment; Germinal products; Registered equine animal; Travelling circus/animal act; Exhibition; Event or activity near borders; Release into the wild; Dispatch centre; Relaying area / purification centre; Ornamental aquaculture establishment; Technical use; Quarantine or similar establishment; Live aquatic animals for human consumption; Other. Which control asks the question is a separate decision, recorded as c-reason-and-additional-details-002; repo-frontend-p8-093 is not overruled, because its placeholder is what is kept.

conflicts.about: The certification question's hint wording.

The fit traces show the hint reading 'This information can be found on the ITAHC.'
The E2E traces show the same older wording, 'This information can be found on the ITAHC.'

conflicts.about: Which commodities are asked the unweaned question.

Any commodity with unweaned options: cattle and pig.

Equines and cattle are in today's catalogue and the re-extracted frontend already asks both; pigs, sheep and goats wait with the MDM commodity catalogue. prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-064 is not overruled: cattle and pig are both still asked, so it still backs what is built and is only incomplete. The expand's title gives no count to check its five entries against (confluence-6497338582-p1-119), so the five listed are taken as the whole rule.

The row completes only once the Additional details page after it is saved too.

Each port of exit option is labelled 'Name (CODE)'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default on how an option reads, and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers it: each option reads '<port name> - <port code>', matching the port of entry options (req-295), while the submitted value stays the code. conflicts.about: The typed form the exit date accepts and the example its hint shows: DD/MM/YYYY with 27/03/2026, or one or two digits for day and month with 'For example, 27/3/2026'.

positions.says: The exit date must be a valid date entered in DD/MM/YYYY format.
The example value given for the exit date is 27/03/2026.
Where V4 specifies a field's format, V4 decides it and the prototype decides how the field reads.
An exit date is accepted in day/month/year form with a four-digit year and one or two digits for day and month.
The exit date hint is 'For example, 27/3/2026'.
The MOJ date picker fills the field as day/month/year without leading zeros, under the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026'.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled. The 11 November ruling puts the format with V4 and how the field reads with the prototype, which splits the hint from the accepted form and leaves the field refusing the very text its own picker writes: the accepted MOJ date picker fills it without leading zeros, so a strict two-digit rule cannot be met by the component the page is built from. Neither reading of 'DD/MM/YYYY', a digit count or the day-month-year order, is ranked above the other.
conflicts.question: Must the exit date be typed with a two-digit day and month, with the hint example 27/03/2026, or is a single-digit day or month still accepted with the hint example 27/3/2026?
conflicts.default: The field keeps the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and accepts a day or month with or without a leading zero, because the accepted date picker fills it that way; V4's DD/MM/YYYY is read as naming the day, month and year order rather than a stricter digit count. If the strict reading is chosen instead, the hint example becomes 27/03/2026 and the picker is configured to write leading zeros, so the field never refuses its own output.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason and additional details pages skips the checks that 'Save and continue' makes.

positions.says: Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue.
No page is an exception to the same-checks rule.
Save and return to overview saves without any validation and goes to the notification hub.
On a hub or review save an invalid or missing follow-up is saved as empty.
On a hub or review save with no reason selected, nothing on the page is changed.
Save and return to overview on additional details saves each answer only if it is one of the offered options and goes to the hub without validating.
When amending, Save and return goes to the review page.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling outranks every other source: on both pages 'Save and return to overview' runs exactly the checks 'Save and continue' runs, keeps the trader on the page with an error for each missing or invalid answer, and shows the overview only when every answer passes. The re-extracted animals frontend already behaves that way on both pages (repo-frontend-p8-117, repo-frontend-p8-137). The ruling withdraws the earlier soft-save decision recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313, so the prototype's save-without-validation claims are overruled. Three claims are left out: prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-076 and prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-077 still say where the button goes when amending and that editing a template saves the template and returns to its review, and prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-078 still backs the purge of other reasons' answers (req-156) even though its saving a missing follow-up as empty is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether the main import reason and additional details pages are also walked in template mode.

positions.says: Template mode is another way of walking through the same journey pages, so these pages are walked in template mode too.
The templates rows stay parked in their own theme and are not built now.
Templates has been dropped for now.

conflicts.outcome: The 4 November and 9 November rulings rank above the 9 October templates ruling, so no template-mode behaviour is built on either page in this programme and req-167 records what was set aside. Nothing is overruled: the 9 October claims still describe how template mode is built whenever templates are picked up again, and the templates area's own records rest on them.

conflicts.about: Whether the destination country and port of exit questions keep the accessible autocomplete the animals frontend now has, or go back to plain selects.

positions.says: A field the prototype shows as a plain select stays a plain select in this programme, the import reason's exit fields included.
The transhipment destination country is one of the three country selects EUDPA-635 does not cover, left in deferred.md for a follow-on ticket.
Every destination country question on the page is already a type-ahead with its own no-match message, and so is every port of exit question.
Without JavaScript every destination country and port of exit is a plain select whose first option reads 'Select one'.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled. The 9 October afternoon ruling's plain-select clause reads two ways: that this programme makes no component change, which leaves in place the autocomplete a follow-on ticket has since added; or that both questions are plain selects, which would take out a built, accessible, tested component with a no-JavaScript fallback. The same ruling left the transhipment destination country to that follow-on ticket, so neither reading is ranked above the other.
conflicts.question: Do the destination country and port of exit questions keep the accessible autocomplete the animals frontend now has, or go back to plain selects as the 9 October afternoon ruling's plain-select clause says?
conflicts.default: Both questions keep the accessible autocomplete exactly as the animals frontend configures it today, with its 'No countries found' and 'No ports found' messages and its plain-select fallback without JavaScript; only the placeholder, the option labels and the order follow the prototype, and nothing is taken out, because removing a built accessible component is not a look-and-feel change the prototype asks for.
